runtime_source_blocks.source: How many images are processed together: fields during mask generation and OPS, or crops per classifier step. For Mask Generation and OPS, 'auto_vram' measures GPU memory on the run data, then divides fields into batches whose sizes differ by at most one. Resident field arrays count toward the memory budget. Use 0 or 'whole' for the earlier largest-fitting-batch estimate, or a positive number to request a field count; it is reduced with a warning if the fields do not fit in memory. Defaults: 'auto_vram' for Mask Generation and OPS, 64 for training.

runtime_source_blocks.source: How many 256-pixel tiles Cellpose passes through the network at once in Mask Generation and OPS. 'auto_vram' measures the GPU working memory and resolves the largest tile batch that fits, up to mask_eval_batch_cap, before segmentation. CPU and external backends use at most 8. Use 0 for one tile per resident field, or a positive number to request the tile batch. The tile batch can move a few mask pixels; resume keeps the recorded value. Default 'auto_vram'.

runtime_source_blocks.source: GPU memory budget in GB for automatic mask batches in Mask Generation and OPS, including resident field arrays and network working memory. Empty uses SPACR_GPU_VRAM_GB when set, then the free card memory. The governor reserves its memory margin and CUDA context and divides the budget among mask workers. Set the same budget to reproduce batch sizes across cards; it can resolve fewer than mask_eval_batch_cap tiles. Default None. Alpha.

private_helper_docs.source:
Give a file the defaults of the version it was written under.

WHY (item 931). A saved settings file or run journal must give the same
result when it is run again, but a file only holds the keys that existed
when it was written. When a later release changes a default, a key the
file never set would silently take the NEW default. Every file spaCR
writes therefore carries ``SETTINGS_VERSION_KEY`` =
``SETTINGS_SCHEMA_VERSION``, and ``DEFAULT_CHANGES`` says, per version,
what a key's default was BEFORE that version. A file with no stamp --
hand-written or older than the stamp -- is read as the oldest version
and gets every old default listed, with a logged notice naming each one
and how to take today's default instead.

TO CHANGE A DEFAULT: add one row to ``DEFAULT_CHANGES``, keyed by the
item number that changes it and holding the OLD default, and raise
``SETTINGS_SCHEMA_VERSION`` to that number. The key must be above every
existing key, because files are already stamped with the current
version; an item whose number is lower takes the next free number and
is listed under that number in docs/source/reproducibility_manifests.rst.
A format-only change instead adds its version to
``SETTINGS_FORMAT_VERSIONS`` and leaves ``DEFAULT_CHANGES`` unchanged.
Version 950 records exact resolved parameters without changing defaults.
933 is item 930's switch of ``ops_align_model`` to ``'tile_affine'``:
it landed after 932, so it could not take 930. 934 is item 937's
``aggregation_defaults`` ``'per_feature'`` (the screen pipeline's
per-feature well table); older files keep ``'legacy'``.
935 is item 940's switch of ``ops_placement_seed_export`` to True: every
solved stitch writes a placement file, and files stamped before keep
it off.
936 is the OPS stage-3 Hybrid profile's ``ops_blas_threads`` (2, was
1) and ``ops_consensus_space`` (``'hybrid'``, was ``'refit'``).
937 is item 941's removal of Gabor and colocalisation from the
``'profiling'`` preset of ``profile_features`` and
``ops_ph_profile_features``: files stamped before get
``profile_optional_families`` and ``ops_ph_profile_optional_families``
with the three families ``'profiling'`` measured then, so their columns
are unchanged.
938 is item 945's ``seg_mask_vram_gb``: the
large-site mask step is sized to 6 GB of card memory, and files stamped
before keep 0, no cap of its own.
940 is item 946's switch of the OPS decode to the proven Funk decode:
``ops_decode_preset`` ``'rule_a_s2'`` (was ``'none'``) and
``ops_decode_threshold_mode`` ``'auto'`` (was ``'manual'``), with
``ops_decode_auto_spot_grid`` back to ``[]`` (calling thresholds only;
files stamped 939 keep item 942's joint grid).
943 is item 965's large-site nuclei (R2): ``seg_cells_from_nucleus_seeds``
``True`` (was ``False``) and ``seg_merge_small_nuclei_frac`` ``0.25``
(was ``0.0``); files stamped before keep the cell model's own cells
and no merge, so their labels are unchanged.
944 is item 966's spacer-prefix decode default: ``ops_read_mode``
empty, which that decode reads as ``'auto'`` while it tunes (was
``'log'``), ``ops_prefix_threshold_tuning`` ``'per_well_decoy'`` (was
``'none'``), ``ops_prefix_decoy_k`` 4 (was 0) and
``ops_prefix_fdr_target_pct`` 1.0 (was 0.1); files stamped before keep
the fixed thresholds and the log read, and the OPS barcode decode reads
an empty ``ops_read_mode`` as ``'log'`` either way.
945 is item 987b's automatic ``batch_size`` of Make Masks (0, the largest
batch that fits the free GPU and RAM; was 50): files stamped before keep
50, so their masks, normalised per batch, are unchanged.
947 is item 967's minority-read rule on the spacer-prefix decode:
``ops_prefix_minority_min_reads`` 3 (was 0, off); files stamped before
keep 0, so every barcode of a cell counts in its call as before.
948 is TASK X's routing of OPS Cellpose through the shared mask tile
batch (``mask_eval_batch_size``; 0 is one tile per field in the resident
batch). Files stamped before get the tile batches the OPS paths always
ran at: ``ops_ph_tile_batch`` 8 (the phenotype path's
``ops_ph_batch_size``, which an old file that sets it keeps, since it is
renamed to this key), ``ops_sbs_tile_batch`` 16 (stitched sequencing
nuclei) and ``spatial_tile_batch`` 16 (Spatial Mask Generation). 946 and
947 belong to other items, so this takes 948.
955 is item 1011's measured VRAM-aware batching for Mask Generation and
OPS: ``batch_size`` and ``mask_eval_batch_size`` now default to
``'auto_vram'``. Files stamped before keep their previous defaults (0
for both since 945), and files before 945 still keep 50 fields. Explicit
values and the older OPS per-path tile defaults remain unchanged.
OPS files before 955 that omit ``randomize`` keep False (acquisition
order); Mask keeps its existing True default. The OPS-only migration
requires known pipeline keys containing ``ops_ph_tile_batch``.
The existing Mask shuffle now uses ``mask_batch_seed`` (42 by default);
the earlier unseeded shuffle had no reproducible order to preserve.

:param settings: the file's settings under today's names, edited in
    place.
:param version: the file's schema version from
    :func:`_settings_file_version`; 0 for an unstamped file.
:param known: the keys the pipeline being run reads, or None for any key.
    A row for another pipeline's key is not added to this one's settings.
    The OPS-only 955 ``randomize`` change requires its pipeline key set.
:returns: ``key -> (old default, version that changed it)`` for every key
    filled in. A key the file sets is never touched. When a key changed
    more than once, the default of the earliest change after ``version``
    is the one the file was written under. An explicit legacy
    ``crop_source`` supplies a missing ``image_source`` before its old
    default is inserted, preserving the requested source mode.

test_doc_inventory.source:
bool -> Toggle/QCheckBox, int -> QSpinBox, float -> QDoubleSpinBox,
enumerated -> combo field, str/None -> _ScalarEdit; each widget starts at
its setting's DEFAULT and a written value is collected back typed.

The traceback reaches the console verbatim when AI is off, when routing
is disabled, or when the AI lookup itself raises; the file-issue button
appears only with consent (and then no report is submitted), and an
unreadable consent preference keeps it hidden.
Set the issue context without submitting a report.

A malformed value leaves a spin box / combo / format field at its
previous value, None clears a text field (never the text "None"), and an
unhandled widget type is a silent no-op. ``AppScreen._truthy`` maps every
CSV spelling of a flag to a bool; ``_ListEdit`` round-trips a Python list
via repr; ``_ScalarEdit`` collects empty as None and text as text.
Match the current registry, count and published alpha summary.
Mask Generation and OPS admit both automatic modes and explicit counts.
CLI coercion and the Qt run boundary accept the shared settings types.
Hiding tuning controls leaves the new Mask and OPS batching defaults active.
Each settings era keeps its original field and tile request.
Folding old defaults never changes a request explicitly saved by the user.
Every new control reaches the panel, tooltip and all three value indices.
Invalid caps fail at validation before either mask application starts.
The settings widgets and CLI retain selectors and parse new numeric controls.
Loading a real saved file folds old defaults before the app fills new ones.
Both GUI settings boundaries can collect the automatic selector.
Apps without a mask plan continue to require numerical minibatches.
Saved settings reach the shared field-order helper with the original app default.
The earlier automatic selector remains explicit and schema 945 keeps its history.
The explicit one-tile-per-field rule and per-path overrides remain available.
Keep the moved GUI refusal admitted without scanning other OPS scopes.
Schema 950 records provenance without inventing a default migration.

Compare parseable tooltip claims with every registered app default.

Most comparisons are exact.  Intentional variants are compared with an
explicit app/setting/value contract above, including a reasoned
classification, so a same-size substitution cannot hide behind a digest.
